wilderness permit: itinerary says no permit required, permit/access say a free self-issue permit is required

before.descent_text: Descend via established rappel routes on the south/east side. Rappel anchors exist on the eastern wall below the summit area. The descent requires technical rope skills and appropriate anchor setup. Alternative descent is to downclimb the South Ridge route if conditions allow.

access.fees: None beyond the parking or entrance fee this route already lists.
access.rules: Group size capped at 12 (people + stock combined) in Glacier Peak Wilderness; larger groups must split with 1-mile separation. Campfires prohibited above 3,500 ft.
access.closures: CLOSED RIGHT NOW: Suiattle River Road (FR 26) is washed out and closed to vehicles at about milepost 4.5 after the December 2025 flood, under a closure order running to 1 January 2028 unless lifted sooner, so the Downey Creek Trailhead cannot be reached by car. The Downey Creek Trail itself is also closed through 31 December 2026 under a separate fire closure. Call the Darrington Ranger District, (360) 436-1155, before planning a trip.
access.seasonal: Mountain Loop Highway has a seasonal gate closure (Deer Creek–Bedal, ~14 mi), typically Nov–mid/late May. Suiattle River Road (FSR 26), the primary Glacier Peak access, has had storm-damage closures — check current conditions before a trip.

access.parking_pass: Northwest Forest Pass required at Mountain Loop Highway trailheads (e.g. Sunrise Mine TH for Vesper Peak) — $5/day or $30/year.

overnight_permit.where: Sign the register at the trailhead. Camping on the North Cascades National Park side of Cache Col needs a park wilderness permit from the Marblemount Wilderness Information Center or Recreation.gov.

emergency.notes: Remote location with 2+ day approach; evacuation is extremely difficult and time-consuming

road.name: Barlow Pass Trailhead, then the gated Monte Cristo Road (foot/bike only) toward the Gunsight Range
road.status: Mountain Loop Highway is paved to Barlow Pass; from there the Monte Cristo Road is gated to vehicles and must be walked or mountain-biked (~4 miles, flat) due to washouts, before continuing on trail into the Glacier Peak Wilderness.
road.driveNote: Roughly 1.5-2 hours from Seattle via US-2/SR-92/Mountain Loop Highway to Barlow Pass; add significant additional hike/bike time on the closed road plus trail beyond Monte Cristo. A Northwest Forest Pass is required at Barlow Pass Trailhead.
road.seasonalGate: Mountain Loop Highway itself is generally open beyond winter, but the Monte Cristo Road has been vehicle-closed long-term due to washout damage.

before.descent_text: The most common descent is via rappel anchors on the eastern wall below the summit area. Alternatively, the route can be downclimbed (care needed on the cannon hole feature). Carry two 60 m ropes — joined, they give rappels of up to a full 60 m. Per-rappel lengths on this descent are not documented, so plan on roughly a pitch each.

rappel_detail.notes: Plan on roughly one pitch. First rappel down the eastern wall, retracing the route.
Caution advised near the 'cannon hole' feature if downclimbing is mixed in instead.
Final rappel reaches the base of the route.

before.rappel_count_note: Route text describes established rappel anchors on the eastern wall with doubled 50m ropes recommended, but gives no rappel-by-rappel breakdown. A count of 3 is inferred from the route's 3-pitch length (rappelling the line itself); the similarly-named South Peak formation at Big Kangaroo reverses its climb in three raps on a single 60m rope. Per-rappel lengths are not documented, so none are given here — plan on roughly one pitch each.

fitnessSpec.hiking: Fit for a long wilderness approach (Dutch Miller Gap or Waptus basin trailheads run well over 15-20 miles round trip with substantial elevation gain before the climbing even starts)
fitnessSpec.packWeight: Overnight/multi-day pack (bivy or backpacking gear) typical, since most parties camp in the Dutch Miller Gap or Waptus basin rather than day-tripping

partner_requirements.approachTime: Long — typically a full day (or more) of hiking from the Dutch Miller Gap or Waptus trailheads just to reach a basin camp, before the summit push itself
requiredSkills: Route-finding on unmarked, slabby terrain with no cairns or established trail
Loose rock management and careful movement to avoid dislodging rock onto partners
Judgment for exposed Class 3-4 moves without a rope
Backcountry navigation (map/compass/GPS) given the remote, lightly-traveled approach
Self-sufficiency for a multi-day wilderness trip far from help
partner_requirements.experienceLevel: Solid Class 3-4 scrambling experience with comfort on loose, blocky, and slabby alpine rock; prior unroped exposure on similar Cascades summits recommended

crowds.peakTraffic: A handful of weekends in August when the Dutch Miller Gap / Waptus approach is fully snow-free
crowds.estimatePerSeason: Roughly 5-15 parties per season, likely fewer in below-average snow years

itinerary.cal: Vista Lakes basin and the summit basin can hold snow well into July, so most parties climb this July-September; the Pete Lake/Cooper Lake road and trailhead are standard Forest Service access with no permit required.

days.note: From the Pete Lake Trailhead on Cooper Lake, hike the flat Pete Lake Trail to Pete Lake (4.5 mi), then join the PCT and climb a long series of switchbacks up to the Vista Lakes tarns just off the trail. It's a long but non-technical day with a full overnight pack.
days.title: Approach to Vista Lakes camp

schedule.label: Leave Pete Lake Trailhead
schedule.detail: Cooper Lake / Salmon La Sac Rd (FR 46) access, ~2,790 ft.

schedule.label: Reach Pete Lake
schedule.detail: Flat trail along the Cooper River.

schedule.label: Join and climb PCT switchbacks
schedule.detail: ~8.5 mi up the Pacific Crest Trail to ~5,500 ft.

schedule.label: Arrive Vista Lakes camp
schedule.detail: Upper lake has sandy/slab sites and swimmable water; ~7.5-8 hr trailhead-to-camp is typical.

days.note: Drop from camp to 5,700 ft Summit Chief Pass, traverse above Summit Chief Lake staying below the ridge/cliffs on the west side, then climb through a high snow basin and up the Southeast Face to a notch on the south ridge. The final ~100 ft is loose Class 2-3 scrambling on untrustworthy rock. Parties describe this as harder than it looks and slower than expected — budget a full day.
days.title: Summit push via Summit Chief Pass and Southeast Face

schedule.label: Leave Vista Lakes camp
schedule.detail: Light daypack; alpine start for a long, complex day.

schedule.label: Summit Chief Pass (5,700 ft)
schedule.detail: Traverse west below the ridge above Summit Chief Lake.

schedule.label: Enter upper basin below the Southeast Face
schedule.detail: Snow fingers and scree lead toward the south ridge notch.

schedule.label: Summit (7,466 ft)
schedule.detail: Roughly 5.5-6 hr camp-to-summit is typical for competent parties; register shows only a handful of ascents per year.

schedule.label: Begin descent
schedule.detail: Reverse the ascent line — loose rock makes downclimbing the crux slow and careful.

schedule.label: Back at Vista Lakes camp
schedule.detail: ~11 hr camp-to-camp round trip is typical.

days.objective: Climb to the summit (7,466 ft) and return to Vista Lakes camp

days.note: Break camp and reverse the approach: down the PCT switchbacks, past Pete Lake, and out along the Cooper River to the trailhead. Straightforward but long with a lighter pack.
days.title: Hike out

itinerary.totalNote: A classic 3-day/2-night backpack: roughly 26-30 miles and ~5,000 ft round trip, with one long, technical summit day from Vista Lakes camp (~11 hr camp-to-camp).
